title: Choose Aperture's visual world
question: The roll assigned Forecast Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Forecast Sheet
options.lineage: Hand-plotted daily weather reports and synoptic charts
options.thesis: Every entry is an observation; over the weeks, your own weather map draws itself.
materials: front symbols: pink half-moons, blue triangles
options.viewport: Today as the day's report: date and conditions at the head, the writing box as the observation form, the last two weeks plotted as a strip of station readings below.
options.risk: Tips into a clinical data dashboard if charts outnumber writing; warmth has to come from colour and hand-plotted line, not more numbers.

raised.raise: Every chart mark encodes a real reading: no decorative isobars, no placeholder data.
A new Echo or an open question stays lit until you have seen it, like a changed gate.
Time runs one way everywhere: oldest left, newest right, on Today, Insights and the session list.
Every explanation sits beside the element it explains, never in a separate manual.

options.label: Riso Zine
options.lineage: Risograph-printed zines and small-press flyers swapped between friends
options.thesis: Each finished entry comes off the press as a two-colour page you would hand to a friend.
options.viewport: Today as a zine cover: a big overprinted date in pink and blue, the writing box as the blank inside page.
options.risk: The obvious home for a pink logo; grain and misregistration read as costume if overused, and it can drift toward cute.

options.label: The Lexicon
options.lineage: Nineteenth-century lexicon pages with a shoulder margin and colour plates
options.thesis: Your journal as a reference book: guide words name the span of dates in view, and colour lives only inside plates.
options.viewport: Entries set like dictionary headwords down one measure; guide words at the head read 'Sep 12 – Oct 31'.
options.case: Fuses well for finding your way through many entries; loses on audience, since friends will not feel at home in a reference book.
options.risk: Cream stock with a text serif is exactly the look most AI journals land on.

options.label: Terminal Signage
options.lineage: International airport wayfinding: yellow sign bands and pictograms
options.thesis: Every screen signs the one next step, so nobody gets lost.
options.viewport: A yellow band over Today names the next step: Write, then End session, then read your summary.
options.case: Directly fixes the 'I don't know what to do' problem; loses on audience, because an airport is the opposite of a quiet place to think.
options.risk: Feels like transit and urgency inside a reflective app, and yellow fights the pink logo.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: Pure black-and-white barcode and sine-lattice data art
options.thesis: Your history as a strobing field of data columns.
options.viewport: A barcode wall of every session, one column each.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cold, clinical, and erases the pink logo.
options.risk: Exactly the clinical feel the brief rules out.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: Boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: Each session as a ticket on a live board.
options.viewport: Today as a departure board of open threads.
options.case: Fuses poorly: travel and departure misread a reflective journal.
options.kept: A change stays lit until you have noticed it.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Your week as a vertical score read upward.
options.viewport: A centre staff with entries as shaped blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an opaque notation is the opposite of an app that must explain itself.
options.kept: Time flows in one direction, everywhere.

options.label: Product Monochrome
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white, every claim proven by a screenshot.
options.viewport: Claim-and-proof sections down a strict grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marketing grammar for an app people write in.
options.kept: Every explanation is paired with the thing it explains.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A calm, minimal writing app like the best-known journals, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: A centred writing column with a quiet sidebar of past entries.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other journaling apps by design.
